title: Something Blue
novel:
The wedding was over, the [[confetti|confetti]] had been [[swept|sweep]] away, and Ted and Robin sat alone at a [[table|table]] in the [[empty|empty]] reception hall. The music had stopped. The lights were low. And between them hung a [[silence|silence]] they had been [[avoiding|avoid]] for months.

"We need to talk," Robin said.

Ted nodded. He had known this moment was coming since the day they [[moved|move]] in together. They loved each other — they really did — but love was not always enough. Robin wanted to see the world, to live in [[Argentina|Argentina]] and [[Japan|Japan]] and places Ted could not [[pronounce|pronounce]]. Ted wanted a family, a house in the [[suburbs|suburb]], a life that looked like the one his parents had — only happier.

"We want different things," Ted said. "And that's nobody's [[fault|fault]]."

"It's no one's fault," Robin repeated, tears [[streaming|stream]] down her cheeks. "So why does it feel so [[awful|awful]]?"

They sat together for a long time, not speaking, just [[holding|hold]] hands. At some point, Marshall came in and saw them and quietly backed out. Lily [[brought|bring]] them a [[plate|plate]] of leftover cake. Barney stood in the doorway for a full minute before walking away without saying a word.

"I don't want to lose you," Robin said.

"You won't," Ted promised. "We'll just be... different. Friend-shaped, instead of love-shaped."

Robin laughed through her tears. "That's the dumbest thing you've ever said."

"I know," Ted said. "I'm a [[mess|mess]]."

They broke up at the wedding of their best friends, on what should have been the happiest day of the year. And somehow it was still beautiful — because sometimes the end of something is also the beginning of something else. Ted did not know it yet, but the woman he would eventually marry was at that wedding too. She was carrying a yellow [[umbrella|umbrella]], and she was standing just outside, in the rain.
